findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is dead logic that unconditionally returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches, so the feature-flag read has no effect and the variable is pointless. The function is effectively `return false`. This is confusing (a reader could think the flag re-enables the feature, and the inverted `!` suggests the opposite of the intent) and is prone to breaking if someone 'fixes' the branch later. Replace with an explicit unconditional rejection (or a correctly polarised flag check) and drop the unused feature lookup.

findings.title: Stub DB silently keeps SQL expression code path alive with runtime errors
findings.body: The new stub `sql.DB` returns "not implemented" from `TablesList`, `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto`. In `SQLCommand.Execute` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:100) this error is placed into `rsp.Error` and `nil` is returned, so the legacy (non-reader) SQL expression path returns a generic opaque "not implemented" to the user instead of a clear 'feature disabled' message. Consider short-circuiting in `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` with an explicit disabled error so behaviour is consistent across both entry points.

findings.title: No test asserting SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This change is a security fix disabling the SQL expression query type, but no test was added verifying that `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error (both with and without the `sqlExpressions` feature flag enabled), nor that `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`SQLCommand.Execute` no longer executes SQL. Without such a test, a future change to `enableSqlExpressions` could silently reintroduce CVE-2024-9264.
